issues.description: Behavior change: _set_base_image now hardcodes python:3.12 instead of empty string, overriding KFP's default
issues.detail: In backend/kale/pipeline.py the fallback was `self.base_image = ""` with a comment explicitly stating 'Use kfp default image'. Changing it to DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE = 'python:3.12' silently overrides whatever KFP would have picked as default for every user who relied on this code path (pod read failures, K8s API exceptions, missing pod). That is a semantic change buried in what was advertised as a UI feature. This belongs in its own patch with its own justification, or revert it and only inject the default at the template layer where the UI actually needs it.

issues.description: Three patches submitted as one. THREE-PATCHES.
issues.detail: This diff does three independent things: (1) introduce a DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE constant and expose it via RPC + template, (2) change the pipeline.py fallback semantics from KFP-default to python:3.12, (3) replace the Input field with a Button+Dialog UI for base image editing. Each has its own risk profile and review surface. The UI rework alone is a significant UX change that has nothing to do with surfacing a default. Split them.

issues.description: DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE constant duplicated in TypeScript with a hardcoded value
issues.detail: The whole point of plumbing get_default_base_image through RPC is to have one source of truth. Then CellMetadataEditor.tsx defines `export const DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE = 'python:3.12'` and Commands.ts hardcodes `return 'python:3.12'` on RPC failure. Now there are three places to update when the default changes (pipeline.py, CellMetadataEditor.tsx, Commands.ts). That defeats the patch. If the RPC fails, fall back to whatever value the component received via props, or show 'unknown' — don't hardcode the version string in the client.

issues.description: Replacing inline Input with a modal Dialog is a regression for editing speed
issues.detail: Before: type the image directly in a 25%-wide Input field inline with the other step controls. After: click a button labeled 'IMAGE', wait for a modal to open, type into the modal Input, click Ok. That is more clicks, more context switches, and slower for the common case of editing a base image. The stated goal is 'display the default base image' — that can be done by setting the Input's placeholder to the default, which the diff already computes. The dialog adds nothing the placeholder couldn't.

issues.description: Button labeled 'IMAGE' with width 5% inside a div padded 0/marginRight 4px — style violates surrounding code's voice
issues.detail: The surrounding controls use Input/Select with sensible widths like 25%/30%/35% and consistent layout. The new control is a contained primary Button sized 'small' with `style={{ width: '5%' }}` wrapped in an ad-hoc div with hand-tuned padding/margin. 5% width on a button labeled IMAGE is going to render strangely and inconsistently. Match the existing layout conventions or commit to redesigning the row coherently.

issues.description: Button disabled on empty stepName but no user feedback explaining why
issues.detail: The new button has `disabled={!(this.props.stepName && this.props.stepName.length > 0)}`. The previous Input had no such gating. Users who could previously set a base image at any time now silently cannot until they name the step. No tooltip, no helper text, just a dead button. Either explain the constraint in the UI or drop the constraint — the underlying updateBaseImage already handles empty stepName via `this.props.stepName || ''`.

issues.description: BAD-TASTE: createBaseImageText now always renders, with special-case isDefault suffix
issues.detail:
The old code returned '' when there was no baseImage. The new code always returns a

, computes an effectiveImage with a 4-level fallback chain, and special-cases `isDefault ? ' (default)' : ''`. That is exactly the kind of accreted special-casing the patch should be cleaning up. If the rule is 'always show the effective image, mark when it's the default', say so once and structure the data accordingly: pass `{ image, source: 'cell'|'pipeline'|'default' }` and render. The current shape will rot.

issues.description: Local `from kale.pipeline import DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE` inside RPC function
issues.detail: rpc/nb.py already imports from kale.pipeline (or could at module level). Doing a function-local import here is either working around a circular import (in which case fix that, don't paper over it) or it's just sloppy. State the reason in a comment if it's intentional; otherwise hoist it.

issues.description: RPC round-trip for a constant that the backend could send once in existing context
issues.detail: We added a new RPC endpoint, a new Commands method with try/catch and a hardcoded fallback, new IProps wiring through three components, and new state in LeftPanel — all to surface a string constant. The backend already returns pipeline/notebook metadata via existing endpoints. Add the default to one of those payloads (or render it server-side in the template, which already has it) and delete the entire RPC + commands path. The patch would be a quarter of the size.

issues.description: Reset to Default button writes '' instead of explicitly clearing — fragile coupling to truthy-check semantics
issues.detail: 'Reset to Default' calls updateBaseImage('') which relies on every downstream consumer treating '' as 'use default'. createBaseImageText uses `this.props.baseImage || ...` which treats '' as falsy and falls through. Fine today, brittle tomorrow — if someone ever stores '' deliberately, or if validation rejects empty strings, this breaks silently. Prefer an explicit null/undefined or a sentinel and a single helper that resolves the effective image.

issues.description: Reordering createBaseImageText and createLimitsText with no stated rationale
issues.detail: InlineMetadata.tsx swaps the order of `createBaseImageText()` and `createLimitsText()` in the render output. Unrelated to the feature. If the visual order matters, justify it in the commit message; if it doesn't, leave it alone. Drive-by reorderings make blame archaeology worse.

issues.description: Width shuffled from 35%/25% to 30%/5% with no holistic layout pass
issues.detail: Changed Select width from 35% to 30% and added a 5%-wide button. Total row layout was not redesigned, just nudged. Either own the row layout or don't touch it.

issues.description: No tests visible for the new behavior
issues.detail: Backend constant, template change, RPC endpoint, fallback semantics change in _set_base_image — none accompanied by tests in the diff. The pipeline.py fallback change in particular is exactly the kind of thing that needs a test pinning the behavior, since it's a silent semantic shift.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK, leaning REFUSE in current shape. The advertised feature is 'display the default base image in the cell metadata UI' — a fine one-line goal. What landed is three patches glued together: a silent semantic change in pipeline.py that overrides KFP's default-image behavior with python:3.12, a UX regression that replaces an inline Input with a modal Dialog behind a tiny IMAGE button, and an RPC round-trip whose stated single-source-of-truth value is then hardcoded in two TypeScript files anyway. Split it: (1) revert the _set_base_image change or send it as its own patch with justification, (2) surface the default by setting the existing Input's placeholder — delete the dialog, the new RPC, the new Commands method, and most of the prop plumbing, (3) if a constant must cross the wire, have exactly one source and fail loud if the RPC fails rather than hardcoding 'python:3.12' on the client. Then resubmit as something a maintainer can land in five minutes.
